name: Mirza Abu Bakr
seoTitle: Mirza Abu Bakr: Mughal Prince in the 1857 Delhi Resistance
seoDescription: Mirza Abu Bakr, a Mughal prince, joined the Delhi rebel coalition during the 1857 uprising against East India Company rule, participating in the resistance that briefly held the city.
role: Mughal prince associated with Delhi resistance in 1857
contribution: Mirza Abu Bakr was part of the Mughal royal family's presence in Delhi during the 1857 rebellion. He participated in the city's defense alongside other royals and rebel commanders through the four-month siege. When British forces retook Delhi in September 1857, he surrendered to officer William Hodson together with Mirza Mughal and Mirza Khizr Sultan. On 22 September 1857, Hodson executed all three princes at Khooni Darwaza — the Bloody Gate in old Delhi — shooting them before a crowd that had gathered expecting the princes to be taken prisoner.
context: North and central India during the anti-colonial uprising of 1857-1859.
impact: The execution at Khooni Darwaza — widely reported and commented upon in British correspondence of 1857 — made the three princes symbols of the violent suppression of the rebellion. Mirza Abu Bakr is remembered in 1857 historiography alongside Mirza Mughal and Mirza Khizr Sultan as part of the Mughal lineage that bore the heaviest personal cost of the rebellion's defeat in Delhi.
